title: SR-Net: Switch
description: Everything the controller reads from the switch itself, over gNMI (gnmic streams every 30 s, the fastest Enterprise SONiC accepts) and SNMP (every 30 s, every 2 s on the ports in use while a run is active): throughput, queue drops, ECN, PFC, buffers, errors, FEC, optics and switch health. Open it from a run page with "Switch view" to land on the run's time range and ports. Generated by gen_switch.py.

list.name: Runs
list.textFormat: Test traffic from the controller's run {{run_id}}

list.name: switch
list.label: Switch
list.description: gNMI target name (the switch's name in the controller, lower-cased by gnmic).

list.name: ports
list.label: Show
list.query: Ports with a host : srnet_switch_port_info,All ports : srnet_switch_up
list.description: Ports with a host: the ports the controller has mapped to a host through LLDP. All ports: every port on the switch.

list.name: port
list.label: Ports
list.description: Pick the switch ports to look at; All means every port in the list (by default the ports with a host). The run page's Switch view button pre-selects the run's ports.

panels.title: Ports up
panels.description: Ports with link, from the SNMP walk every 30 s.

panels.title: Total in
panels.description: Sum of the selected ports' ingress, 2 minute rate.

panels.title: Queue drops /s
panels.description: Packets dropped in egress queues of the selected ports. Any value above 0 under load means the fabric is lossy for that traffic.

panels.title: PFC pause /s
panels.description: Priority flow control pause frames received plus sent. 0 on this fabric means PFC is off or never needed.

panels.title: CRC errors /s
panels.description: Frames failing the CRC: a bad cable or optic.

panels.title: Hottest sensor
panels.description: Hottest of the switch's temperature sensors (CPU, ASIC, inlet, outlet and so on).

panels.title: Hottest optic
panels.description: Hottest transceiver among the selected ports (module case temperature).

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the switch last booted. Red only in the first hour after a reboot.

panels.title: Ingress Gbps per port (gNMI, 30 s)
panels.description: Bytes received by the switch on each port. gNMI samples every 30 s (the fastest Enterprise SONiC accepts), so short bursts are averaged.

targets.expr: (rate({__name__=~"srnet_gnmi_.*interface_state_counters_in_octets",source=~"(?i)$switch",interface_name=~"$port"}[2m]) keep_metric_names * 8 / 1e9) * on(interface_name) group_left(host, host_port, fabric) max by (interface_name, host, host_port, fabric) (label_replace(srnet_switch_port_info{switch=~"(?i)$switch"}, "interface_name", "$1", "port", "(.*)")) or (rate({__name__=~"srnet_gnmi_.*interface_state_counters_in_octets",source=~"(?i)$switch",interface_name=~"$port"}[2m]) keep_metric_names * 8 / 1e9) unless on(interface_name) max by (interface_name, host, host_port, fabric) (label_replace(srnet_switch_port_info{switch=~"(?i)$switch"}, "interface_name", "$1", "port", "(.*)"))

(rate({__name__=~"srnet_gnmi_.*interface_state_counters_out_octets",source=~"(?i)$switch",interface_name=~"$port"}[2m]) keep_metric_names * 8 / 1e9) * on(interface_name) group_left(host, host_port, fabric) max by (interface_name, host, host_port, fabric) (label_replace(srnet_switch_port_info{switch=~"(?i)$switch"}, "interface_name", "$1", "port", "(.*)")) or (rate({__name__=~"srnet_gnmi_.*interface_state_counters_out_octets",source=~"(?i)$switch",interface_name=~"$port"}[2m]) keep_metric_names * 8 / 1e9) unless on(interface_name) max by (interface_name, host, host_port, fabric) (label_replace(srnet_switch_port_info{switch=~"(?i)$switch"}, "interface_name", "$1", "port", "(.*)"))

panels.title: Port Gbps during runs (SNMP, 2 s)
panels.description: While a run is active the controller polls the ports that are up every 2 s over SNMP; between runs every 30 s. This is the view to compare with the host NIC counters second by second. Idle ports are left out.

panels.title: Utilisation (% of line rate)
panels.description: Ingress and egress rate against the port's configured speed (ifHighSpeed, from SNMP). A 100G port carrying 98 Gbps is at 98%. Idle ports are left out.

panels.title: Average frame size (bytes)
panels.description: Octets divided by packets received. RDMA at 4096 MTU shows about 4 kB; small values mean control traffic or fragmentation.

targets.expr: sum by (interface_name) (rate({__name__=~"srnet_gnmi_.*interface_state_counters_in_octets",source=~"(?i)$switch",interface_name=~"$port"}[2m]) keep_metric_names) / sum by (interface_name) (rate({__name__=~"srnet_gnmi_.*interface_state_counters_in_pkts",source=~"(?i)$switch",interface_name=~"$port"}[2m]) keep_metric_names) > 0

panels.title: Queue drops per second
panels.description: Packets dropped per egress queue (tail drops and WRED drops); queues that dropped nothing are left out. The 400G to 100G step from the 770AP into the Sparks shows here as queue 0 drops on the Spark ports.

panels.title: ECN marked per second
panels.description: Packets ECN-marked by WRED; unmarked queues are left out. Nothing here under congestion means ECN is not configured on the queue, so RoCE congestion control never kicks in and the NIC retransmits after drops instead.

panels.title: Transmit packets per queue
panels.description: Which queue carries the traffic (idle queues left out). RoCE should sit in the lossless queue (3 on a classic profile); everything in queue 0 means no DSCP-to-queue map is applied.

panels.title: Queue watermark (% of buffer)
panels.description: Peak egress queue occupancy in the last sample window, as a share of the shared buffer; queues at 0 are left out. Sustained values near 100 precede drops.

panels.title: Queue watermark (bytes)
panels.description: Peak egress queue occupancy in bytes since the counter was last read (queues at 0 left out).

panels.title: Ingress priority-group watermark (%)
panels.description: Shared and headroom buffer use per ingress priority group (groups at 0 left out). Headroom use above 0 means PFC was asserted and the buffer absorbed in-flight data.

panels.title: PFC pause frames received per second
panels.description: Pause frames the switch received from hosts (the host asked the switch to stop), per priority.

panels.title: PFC pause frames sent per second
panels.description: Pause frames the switch sent to hosts (the switch asked the host to stop), per priority.

panels.title: PFC enabled per priority
panels.description: One row per port, one column per priority: on or off. RoCE needs PFC on for its priority (3 on a classic profile) on every port it crosses.

panels.title: PFC watchdog
panels.description: PFC watchdog counters, one row per port and queue. storm_detected above 0 means a port was stuck sending pause and the watchdog cut it off.

panels.title: CRC errors per second
panels.description: Any CRC error at steady rate points at the cable or the optic on that port. Compare with the host's symbol errors on the same leg.

targets.expr: (rate({__name__=~"srnet_gnmi_.*ethernet.*in_crc_errors",source=~"(?i)$switch",interface_name=~"$port"}[2m]) keep_metric_names) * on(interface_name) group_left(host, host_port, fabric) max by (interface_name, host, host_port, fabric) (label_replace(srnet_switch_port_info{switch=~"(?i)$switch"}, "interface_name", "$1", "port", "(.*)")) or (rate({__name__=~"srnet_gnmi_.*ethernet.*in_crc_errors",source=~"(?i)$switch",interface_name=~"$port"}[2m]) keep_metric_names) unless on(interface_name) max by (interface_name, host, host_port, fabric) (label_replace(srnet_switch_port_info{switch=~"(?i)$switch"}, "interface_name", "$1", "port", "(.*)"))

panels.title: Malformed frames per second
panels.description: Fragments and undersize frames: a bad link. Oversize and jabber: an MTU mismatch (a 9000 byte frame into a 1500 byte port). Ports without any are left out.

panels.title: Discards and errors (SNMP)
panels.description: Interface-level discards (buffer full) and errors from IF-MIB; ports without any are left out. Out discards on a 100G port fed from a 400G port are the speed-mismatch drops.

panels.title: FEC and link state
panels.description: Per port: the FEC in use (RS-FEC is required at 100G and above over copper and most optics) and the configured speed. This SONiC build does not expose FEC corrected or uncorrected codeword counters, so pre-FEC bit error rate is not available; CRC errors are the post-FEC signal.

panels.title: Ingress frame sizes
panels.description: Histogram of received frame sizes as rates (empty buckets left out). RDMA traffic at MTU 4096 lands in the 2048 to 4095 bucket; 9000 byte MTU in 8192 and up.

panels.title: Transceiver temperature
panels.description: Module case temperature from the switch side DOM. Most QSFP and OSFP modules alarm at 70 to 75 C.

panels.title: Receive power per lane (dBm)
panels.description: Average optical receive power per lane, from the module total the switch reports (mW over all media lanes) divided by the lane count. Healthy DR and FR optics sit around -4 to +4 dBm per lane. A drop on one port means a dirty connector or a failing far-end laser.

panels.title: Transmit power per lane (dBm)
panels.description: Average optical transmit power per lane, derived the same way as receive power.

panels.title: Laser bias current (module total, as reported)
panels.description: The switch reports one bias figure per module, apparently summed over the lanes, so read it as a trend: rising bias at constant output power is a laser ageing out.

panels.title: CPU and memory
panels.description: Control-plane CPU and memory. Telemetry streaming itself costs a little CPU; a busy CPU does not slow the data plane but delays counters.

panels.title: Temperature sensors
panels.description: Every TEMP sensor the switch reports (ASIC, inlet, outlet, CPU) against the lowest high-threshold.

panels.title: Fan speed
panels.description: Every fan the switch reports, in RPM. One fan well below its tray mates is failing; all of them climbing means the switch is running hot.

panels.title: Fans and PSUs OK
panels.description: 1 = present and operating, 0 = failed or missing.

panels.title: gNMI series per switch
panels.description: How many distinct series gnmic delivered in the last two minutes. A drop to 0 means the stream died (see the Switches page).
